newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas falls sharply as Q3 97 sold down heavily.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas falls sharply as Q3 97 sold down heavily.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices fell on Friday as heavy selling in the third quarter brought prices down and had a knock on effect on all other periods, traders and brokers said.

One seller in particular was reported selling heavily in Q3. Around eight deals were said done between 9.40 pence and 9.65 pence a therm, although not all of these were confirmed and some were only rumoured.
"It all started with Q3," said a broker, "that came down so then Q4 came down because it had to, so then Q1 came down, so then the gas year came down."

A trader said there was only one seller in the third quarter willing to sell below 9.50 pence a therm, but this was done several times and "it had a ripple effect on to the rest of the year," he added.
Traders also cited the arrival of extra volumes of J-Block gas and the Transco storage tender as bearish factors in the market.

Apart from the third quarter, there were several trades done in the gas year from October at between 12.40 pence and 12.60 pence a therm, and several in the first quarter between 16.30 pence and 16.50 pence.
Other periods did not see such a heavy volume of trade, but there was solid trade in all periods from this weekend until summer 1998, almost all at lower prices.

The weakness in the third quarter was reflected on the IPE futures market where 9.50 pence was done in both July and August, down by 0.30 pence a therm or more from the previous settlement level. A total of 95 lots were done in four separate trades.
